A shopper in China has secured a two-bedroom apartment for just $1.70 (11 yuan) during the country's annual Double 11 shopping festival. The 68-square-metre property in Heilongjiang province attracted 1,677 bidders on Alibaba Auction, with the winning buyer claiming the capped price.  According to the South China Morning Post, the buyer plans to use the apartment as a winter holiday retreat rather than a permanent home.  However, the bargain comes with an additional cost of around 2,000 yuan ($300) in deed taxes to complete the ownership transfer, while legal experts warn buyers to check for hidden fees and ownership issues. #china #house #asia #hardnews

China's Qwen 4 is finally here. Alibaba just launched Qwen4-Max, its new flagship AI model, at $1.50 per million input tokens and $4.50 output, compared with $4 and $20 for Claude Opus 5.5. Alibaba says it uses half the tokens of its last model and cuts the cost per task by 62%. But on its own chart, it only wins four of 16 tests, while Claude Opus 5.5 wins seven, and the chart skips Fable 5.2 and Gemini 4 Carbon. It's not open source either, though smaller Qwen4 models will be later. Would you switch to a cheaper model that's almost as good?
